newsitem.title: USA: Education Alternatives to receive payment.
newsitem.headline: Education Alternatives to receive payment.

text.p: Education Alternatives Inc said Tuesday it expects to receive an additional $3.2 million payment resulting from the cancellation of its Hartford, Conn., school management contract.
Under a proposed settlement, the company will receive the $3.2 million in annual installments of $650,000, beginning in July 1997. That will bring the total Hartford settlement to $6.3 million.
The company said it already received $3.1 million for computers installed and capital improvements made to the Hartford schools.
Education Alternatives said it and Hartford officials also agreed to release each other from any further claims.

The settlement is subject to the execution of a definitive agreement. The company said it expects to conclude these negotiations in the near future but added there can be no assurance a final agreement will be reached on terms satisfactory to it.

Earlier, Education Alternatives reported a net loss for the fourth quarter of $0.15 a share, compared with a loss of $0.98 a year ago. For fiscal 1996, it reported a net loss of $1.27 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $1.09.
The company said the cancellation of contracts in Hartford and Baltimore, Md., affected its results.

"While the cancellations of the Hartford and Baltimore contracts have been disappointing, we are pleased that we have basically resolved all remaining disputes under these contracts," John Golle, chairman, said in a statement.
He added the private school business reported improved profits in fiscal 1996 and the company expects to pursue additional opportunities in this market through growth and acquisitions.
